messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime-streaming.p95 > SLO (1200ms) in us-east-1 for last 5m. P99 = 5.6s. Elevated error budget burn. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:
Ajay: ack. I'm on it. Paging SRE rotation. grabbing dashboards now.
Maria: I see a spike around 14:07 UTC — top sig is 'sse_proxy_write_timeout' from edge-proxy-12. Connection count up ~3.2x.
Tim: logs show a lot of stalled chunk writes: `EPIPE` and lots of 504s from proxy -> runtime. tracespoint id=stream.chunk.write.delay
Emma: any customer-reported impact? CS queue has 3 tickets referencing slow live updates (dashboard lagging).
Sara: Customer "EduLearn" reported live lecture captions delayed ~10s and occasional reconnects. They are on eu and us-east.
Ajay: hypothesis: slow consumer backpressure combined with proxy write buffer growth causing proxy to hit keepalive/timeout thresholds, which cascades into higher tail latency.
Leo: can we confirm client ack rates? metrics: `sse.consumer_read_rate` per connection dropping. slow consumers = top signal.
Tim: copying relevant snippet from proxy logs:
```
2026-03-15T14:07:12Z proxy-edge-12 write_blocked conn=54212 buffer=1.8MB stall_ms=4300
2026-03-15T14:07:14Z proxy-edge-12 write_timeout conn=54212 reason=slow_consumer
2026-03-15T14:07:15Z proxy-edge-12 upstream_504 req=xyz runtime=call timeout
```
Ajay: immediate mitigation options: 1) enable aggressive flush/shorter chunk timeout (30s->10s) 2) trigger per-connection backpressure drop for connections exceeding write buffer 3) scale proxy pool (add 3 nodes) 4) failover customer traffic to eu region for impacted accounts. Which do we do now?
Maria: scaling proxies is fairly quick (spin + rebal), but won't help slow consumers. Short-term config change to lower `chunk_write_timeout` from 30s to 8s will free resources faster. I can push that to staging then prod with 1min rollout.
Tim: also reduce server-side output buffer size for SSE to 256KB. That forces backpressure earlier and prevents huge buffers.
Emma: for customer comms, propose: "We observed transient streaming delays affecting live updates for a subset of customers. We're applying mitigations now and will follow up with root cause." Want me to post an initial status?
Ajay: yes. Emma post a brief status on status.redwood.ai and tag EduLearn CSM. Include ETA 30m for mitigation check.
Emma: posting now. Status: "Investigating increased streaming tail latency in us-east; mitigation in progress. Some live sessions may experience delayed chunks or reconnects." :white_check_mark:
Ajay: I'm going to apply the config changes: Maria please prepare a short, targeted prod rollout (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%) and Tim coordinate the runtime buffer change.
Maria: starting canary deploy of `proxy-config v2026.03.15-1` to 10% (edge-proxy pool). Rolling out now.
Tim: prepping runtime flag `--sse-output-buffer=262144` and `--chunk-write-timeout=8s`. I will stage on a single runtime host and monitor p95/p99.
Ajay: monitoring dashboards: watch `realtime-streaming.p95`, `proxy.write_latency`, `sse.consumer_read_rate`, `edge_conn_count`. Also check error budget burn.
Maria: canary 10% applied at 14:18 UTC. No immediate regressions.
Tim: runtime change applied to canary host at 14:20. Observed 35% drop in per-conn buffer growth for canary traffic.
Ajay: nice. Maria, continue to 50% if Tim sees no issues for 5m.
Maria: moving to 50% at 14:26.
Tim: hold — I'm seeing a small uptick in reconnect events for very high-frequency clients on canary (clients that rely on large buffers). It's within expected tradeoff but flagging.
Leo: notes: these clients are mostly internal dashboards and some EduLearn rooms. Could we apply a targeted exception for known good clients?
Ajay: yes, use allowlist for large-buffer clients for next 30m while we notify them about graceful downgrade. But default must stay strict. Maria, can the canary config include an allowlist?
Maria: yes, adding allowlist for `edu-*` and `internal-monitoring` prefixes. Updating canary now.
Emma: updated customer comms: added note that some live sessions may see intermittent reconnects during mitigations. CSM looped in.
Ajay: metrics after 50% rollout: p95 down from 1.2s -> 420ms, p99 down from 5.6s -> 1.1s. Error budget burn reduced. Good signal.
Tim: keep an eye on reconnects; we may need to tune client retry backoff to avoid thundering herd. Add temporary jitter if not present.
Ajay: for triage notes: root cause likely interplay of slow consumer backpressure + proxy buffer growth + aggressive upstream keepalive timeouts. Longer-term: server-driven flow control (explicit client ack), better observability on per-connection drain, and adaptive chunk sizing.
Emma: is oncall handoff needed? My shift ends in 40m.
Ajay: yes, I'll handoff to Leo in 30m. Action items for next oncall (Leo): 1) monitor p95/p99 for next 2 hours, 2) finalize exception allowlist removal plan, 3) coordinate with SDK team on client-side retry/backoff, 4) follow up with EduLearn CSM with RCA draft later.
Leo: ack. I'll be ready to take over. Please add a short handoff summary and flags.
Ajay: handoff summary:
- incident id: 2026-03-15-stream-tailspin-01
- root cause (probable): slow consumers causing proxy write buffer growth -> timeouts -> cascading tail latency
- mitigations applied: reduced chunk_write_timeout (30s->8s), reduced SSE output buffer (universal 256KB), proxy pool +3 nodes, targeted allowlist for heavy-buffer clients
- customer impact: EduLearn and a handful of internal dashboards experienced delayed chunks (10s) and occasional reconnects; mitigations reduced p95/p99 and stabilized traffic
- follow-ups: implement adaptive flow-control, add per-connection drain metrics, SDK retry guidance, post-incident RCA

Ajay: tagging Leo and Sara for handoff. @Leo @Sara please ack once you're in.
Leo: ack — I have context. I'll monitor for 2h and liaise with SDK and CS.
Sara: ack. I'll coordinate with EduLearn CSM and confirm they saw improvements.
Emma: closing status update to customers in 30m after we verify stability.
incident-bot: Incident 2026-03-15-stream-tailspin-01 acknowledged by Ajay and handed to Leo. Severity: Sev2.
Leo: leaving final note — if p99 creeps above 2s or reconnects > 1% of connections, escalate to Sev1 and call infra oncall.
Ajay: thanks all. handing off.
